description: Intent i002 (SNAPSHOT=s01, BRANCH=xsk-umem-rings) complete. One medium-confidence finding: include/net/xdp_sock_drv.h:276-280 (__xsk_buff_get_metadata) — the function validates the UMEM-resident struct xsk_tx_metadata flags field once via xsk_buff_valid_tx_metadata() ('!(meta->flags & ~XDP_TXMD_FLAGS_VALID)') but then returns the raw shared-memory pointer 'meta' instead of a cached snapshot (quote literal at lines 276-280). Every downstream consumer therefore re-fetches flags and request fields from user-writable AF_XDP UMEM: in include/net/xdp_sock.h:178-181 xsk_tx_metadata_request() gates on a second independent read of meta->flags and separately loads meta->request.csum_start/csum_offset into the tmo_request_checksum(u16 csum_start, u16 csum_offset) driver hook, with no READ_ONCE, no local copy, and no lock between the validation fetch and the consumption fetch — the direct structural analogue of the seed's xsk_skb_metadata() TOCTOU. Consumption sites audited: igc_main.c:3077/3085, mlx5 en/xsk/tx.c:102, libeth include/net/libeth/xsk.h:199-208. Classified candidates: TX-ring descriptors are safe (net/xdp/xsk_queue.h:246 copies struct xdp_desc by value once and validates the local copy); mlx5 and libeth callbacks ignore the offset arguments (safe); igc is reported as the consumption site but registers no tmo_request_checksum, so only launch_time reaches driver code there — hence medium confidence: the single-fetch invariant is demonstrably violated by the return-pointer API, but no s01 driver was found that consumes the re-fetched csum offsets as a memory offset. The seed's own xsk_skb_metadata() (net/xdp/xsk.c:761-798, still unfixed in s01) is excluded as never reportable. Bounded limitations: only the xsk-umem-rings branch of net/xdp + TX-metadata driver consumers was searched; setup/ioctl paths were skimmed, not exhaustively line-audited; no compilation or dynamic testing was performed; vhost, TPACKET, and io_uring paths are out of scope for this intent.
